nodes.title: Terms, State Functions & Properties
points: System: Part of universe chosen for thermodynamic study. Open (exchanges matter & energy), Closed (exchanges energy only), Isolated (exchanges neither matter nor energy).
State Function: Property whose value depends solely on initial and final states of system, independent of path (P, V, T, U, H, S, G).
Path Function: Property whose value depends on the path followed (Work W, Heat Q).
Extensive Property: Depends on the amount of matter present (Mass, Volume, Internal energy U, Enthalpy H, Entropy S, Heat capacity).
Intensive Property: Independent of the amount of matter present (Temperature, Pressure, Density, Refractive index, Surface tension, Viscosity, Specific heat, Melting/Boiling point).

formulas.label: Extensive properties
formulas.expr: Additive properties (V, m, U, H, S, G)

formulas.label: Intensive properties
formulas.expr: Non-additive properties (T, P, ρ, K_b, K_f)

nodes.title: Thermodynamic Processes & PV-Work
points: Processes: Isothermal (ΔT = 0, ΔU = 0), Isobaric (ΔP = 0), Isochoric (ΔV = 0, W = 0), Adiabatic (Q = 0).
Reversible Process: Occurs in infinite steps, driving force infinitesimally greater than opposing force, maximum work obtained, reversible at any stage.
Irreversible Process: Occurs rapidly in finite steps, non-equilibrium, real spontaneous processes.
Pressure-Volume Work: W = −P_ext ΔV = −P_ext (V₂ − V₁).
IUPAC Sign Convention: Work done ON system (compression) W > 0; Work done BY system (expansion) W < 0. Heat absorbed by system Q > 0; Heat released Q < 0.
Conversion: 1 L·bar = 100 J; 1 L·atm = 101.3 J.

nodes.title: Maximum Work in Isothermal Reversible Expansion
points: For n moles of an ideal gas expanding isothermally and reversibly from V₁ to V₂ (or P₁ to P₂):
Formula: W_max = −2.303 n R T log₁₀(V₂ / V₁) = −2.303 n R T log₁₀(P₁ / P₂).
R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
Since V₂ > V₁ in expansion, W_max is negative (work done by the system).
Work in Free Expansion: In vacuum (P_ext = 0) ⟹ W = 0 for any expansion.

formulas.label: W_max volume formula
formulas.expr: W_max = −2.303 n R T log₁₀(V₂ / V₁)

formulas.label: W_max pressure formula
formulas.expr: W_max = −2.303 n R T log₁₀(P₁ / P₂)

nodes.title: First Law of Thermodynamics & Applications
points: Statement: Energy of universe is constant; it can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
Mathematical Formulation: ΔU = Q + W.
Applications to Processes:
1. Isothermal (ΔU = 0): Q = −W (all heat absorbed is converted into work).
2. Adiabatic (Q = 0): ΔU = W_ad (work done at expense of internal energy).
3. Isochoric (ΔV = 0 ⟹ W = 0): ΔU = Q_v (heat absorbed at constant volume equals increase in internal energy).
4. Isobaric (ΔP = 0): ΔU = Q_p − P ΔV ⟹ Q_p = ΔU + P ΔV = ΔH.

nodes.title: Enthalpy (H) & Relation with Internal Energy
points: Enthalpy Definition: Total heat content of system at constant pressure: H = U + PV.
Enthalpy Change: ΔH = ΔU + P ΔV (at constant P).
Relation between ΔH and ΔU for gaseous reactions:
ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g R T, where Δn_g = ∑ n_g(products) − ∑ n_g(reactants).
Rules for Δn_g (COUNT GASES ONLY!):
1. If Δn_g = 0 ⟹ ΔH = ΔU.
2. If Δn_g > 0 ⟹ ΔH > ΔU.
3. If Δn_g < 0 ⟹ ΔH < ΔU.

nodes.title: Hess's Law & Enthalpy of Reactions
points: Hess's Law of Constant Heat Summation: The overall enthalpy change for a chemical reaction is the same whether it takes place in one step or in several steps.
Standard Enthalpy of Reaction from Formation Enthalpies:
Δ_r H° = ∑ Δ_f H°(products) − ∑ Δ_f H°(reactants).
Standard enthalpy of formation of pure elements in their reference standard state is ZERO: Δ_f H°(O₂, C_graphite, N₂, H₂, Fe) = 0.
Enthalpy of Reaction from Bond Enthalpies:
Δ_r H° = ∑ Bond Enthalpies(reactants broken) − ∑ Bond Enthalpies(products formed). (Reactants minus Products!).

formulas.label: Δ_r H° from formation
formulas.expr: Δ_r H° = ∑ Δ_f H°(products) − ∑ Δ_f H°(reactants)

nodes.title: Entropy (S) & Second Law of Thermodynamics
points: Entropy (S): Thermodynamic measure of molecular disorder, randomness, or chaos of a system. State function, extensive property.
Entropy Change: ΔS = Q_rev / T. SI Unit: J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
Entropy increases in: Solid ⟶ Liquid ⟶ Gas; dissolution of solute; decomposition reactions; increase in temperature.
Second Law of Thermodynamics: The total entropy of the universe increases in any spontaneous (natural) process:
ΔS_total = ΔS_system + ΔS_surroundings > 0 (for spontaneous process).
At equilibrium: ΔS_total = 0.
Third Law of Thermodynamics: The entropy of a perfectly crystalline substance is ZERO at absolute zero temperature (0 K).

nodes.title: Gibbs Free Energy (G) & Spontaneity Criteria
points: Gibbs Free Energy Definition: G = H − TS. State function, extensive property.
Gibbs-Helmholtz Equation: ΔG = ΔH − T ΔS (at constant T and P).
Spontaneity Criteria based on ΔG:
1. ΔG < 0: Process is SPONTANEOUS (exergonic).
2. ΔG = 0: System is at EQUILIBRIUM.
3. ΔG > 0: Process is NON-SPONTANEOUS (endergonic).
Temperature Dependence of Spontaneity:
• ΔH < 0, ΔS > 0 ⟹ ΔG always < 0 (Spontaneous at all T).
• ΔH > 0, ΔS < 0 ⟹ ΔG always > 0 (Non-spontaneous at all T).
• ΔH < 0, ΔS < 0 ⟹ Spontaneous at LOW T (T < ΔH/ΔS).
• ΔH > 0, ΔS > 0 ⟹ Spontaneous at HIGH T (T > ΔH/ΔS).
Equilibrium Constant Link: ΔG° = −2.303 R T log₁₀ K_eq.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & State Functions
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive expression for maximum work done in isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gas: W_max = −2.303 nRT log₁₀(V₂/V₁).
Board Favourite #2: Derive relation between ΔH and ΔU for a gaseous reaction: ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT.
Board Favourite #3: State First, Second, and Third Laws of Thermodynamics.
Board Favourite #4: State Hess's Law of Constant Heat Summation with an illustrative example.
Board Favourite #5: Define: (1) Standard enthalpy of formation, (2) Bond enthalpy, (3) State function vs Path function, (4) Intensive vs Extensive property.

formulas.label: ΔH proof
formulas.expr: ΔH = ΔU + Δ(PV) = ΔU + PΔV = ΔU + Δn_g RT

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Sign Traps & Δn_g Hacks
points: Δn_g Calculation Rule: Count ONLY GASEOUS moles! Completely ignore solids and liquids.
Example 1: CaCO₃(s) ⟶ CaO(s) + CO₂(g) ⟹ Δn_g = 1 − 0 = +1 (ΔH > ΔU).
Example 2: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⟶ 2NH₃(g) ⟹ Δn_g = 2 − (1 + 3) = −2 (ΔH < ΔU).
Bond Enthalpy Hack: Remember it is Reactants MINUS Products: Δ_r H° = ∑ BE(reactants) − ∑ BE(products) (unlike formation enthalpies which are products − reactants!).
Equilibrium Temperature Shortcut: When a reaction transitions from non-spontaneous to spontaneous, set ΔG = 0 ⟹ T = ΔH / ΔS.
IUPAC Work Sign Trap: Expansion work is ALWAYS negative (−); compression work is positive (+).

formulas.label: Bond energy vs formation
formulas.expr: BE = Reactants − Products | Δ_f H = Products − Reactants
